literal: Those of evil deeds fear not; the excellent ones will fear the arrogance called evil deed.
translation: Those accustomed to evil do not fear it, but the noble deeply fear the arrogance of committing evil deeds.
modern: தீய செயல்களைச் செய்பவர்கள் தீவினை என்னும் செருக்கைக் கண்டு அஞ்ச மாட்டார்கள். ஆனால் சிறந்த பண்புடையவர்கள் அதற்கு அஞ்சுவார்கள்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts the attitudes of two types of people towards wrongdoing. Those who already commit evil deeds do not fear the arrogance and destructive pride that comes with doing evil. In contrast, noble and excellent people deeply fear this arrogance, knowing its harmful consequences. The word 'cerukku' (arrogance or infatuation) highlights that evil is not just an action, but a blinding pride that the wise actively avoid.
